column1: # Per-probe result of the selfhost compiler against the Go reference, one row per
# file in selfhost/tests/probes. A run that does not reproduce these exact statuses
# fails: a pass set that can shrink silently is not a gate, and a recorded
# disagreement that quietly starts passing means the baseline stopped describing
# stage -- the probe as a module of the staged selfhost package, linked and executed;
# ok | mismatch (wrong answer) | refused (the backend declines the shape)
# A probe entry returns i64 because that is what the driver can call. A function
# returning !T has no i64 ABI, and an i64 function cannot unwrap an error union, so a
# probe of the error-union shapes names them on a `// probe-reach:` line instead: the
# staged root and the probe's own main reach them with `try`, which is what gets them
# lowered, and the driver still reads only the probe's own entry.
